title: Normal stalks of relative normalization in a locally Noetherian normal source
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $X$ locally Noetherian (every affine open has a Noetherian section ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Assume that every stalk $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a domain and integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For the relative normalization $f.\mathrm{normalization}$ of $Y$ in $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], every stalk is a domain and integrally closed in its fraction field. No integrality or connectedness assumption on $X$ or $Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 035L (lemma-normal-normalization), normality clause, using local Noetherianness for the finite-component hypothesis; proof uses Tags 0357, 0358, 034L.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood U of the image of a point z of the relative normalization. Its inverse image in X is quasi-compact by QuasiCompact f and affine-open compactness. Apply [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] to identify its ring of sections with a finite product of normal domains.

Let V be the inverse image of U in the normalization. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], V is affine and normalizationObjIso identifies its section ring with the integral closure of Γ(Y,U) in Γ(X,f⁻¹U). Apply [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product] to obtain normality of all prime localizations of this closure.

Let p be the prime of Γ(V) belonging to z, and map p across normalizationObjIso. Localization.localRingEquiv identifies the prime localizations of these isomorphic rings. The affine-open localization theorem identifies the stalk at z with the localization at p via IsLocalization.algEquiv. Compose these ring equivalences and transport IsDomain and IsIntegrallyClosed, proving the unchanged assertion. Empty charts have no points; all other edge cases are retained.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof: finite normal component sections, integral closure normal prime localizations, and affine stalk transport. The integral-source normalization theorem is not used.

lean.statement:
theorem relativeNormalization_normal_stalks {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (hX : ∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∀ z : f.normalization, IsDomain (f.normalization.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (f.normalization.presheaf.stalk z)
